Command-Line Reference Overview

This section is the reference manual for all CLI commands of the Sla compiler plugin. After reading this page you will know which commands exist, the several equivalent invocation forms, and the responsibility boundaries of each command; the following pages give the syntax, parameters, and output locations for each command.

Invocation forms: the top-level sla command is preferred

sla is a top-level command: after installation, sla.exe sits alongside sa.exe in the bin directory on PATH, and all functionality can be written directly as sla <command>, without going through the host prefix. It comes from two sources: the fully automatic installer bundle ships bin\sla.exe; or, in the source tree, running the plugin's tools/install_windows.ps1 (which internally copies the built sla.exe into SCI's bin directory).

FormExampleDescription
sla <command>sla check main.slaRecommended form. A standalone top-level command; an internal argument-rewriting layer converts it into the plugin invocation form, ultimately entering the same command dispatcher.
sa sla <command>sa sla check main.slaInvoked through the SA host in plugin-command form, with exactly equivalent effect; suitable for environments where only the plugin is installed and there is no standalone sla.exe.
sla slab <subcommand> / sa slab <subcommand>sla slab build main.slaA short alias for the three sab subcommands (build / workspace / disasm).
Equivalence ruleThe examples used in the following pages of this section are mostly written as sa sla … (consistent with the usage lines in the plugin source). Wherever you see sa sla xxx, you can replace it verbatim with the top-level sla xxx — just drop the sa prefix; the arguments stay the same.
NoteA plugin installed via sa plugin install --dev is in development mode, and the host requires the relevant commands to run with SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1; a formal installation via the installer bundle or install_bundle_windows.ps1 does not need this prefix. See the “Environment Variables” page in this section for details.

How to obtain the top-level sla command

MethodActionResult
Fully automatic installer bundle (recommended)See “Getting Started → Installation and Building”: run install_bundle_windows.ps1 -Bundle SCI-windows-x64-full.zip, or use the graphical installerThe bin directory gets both sa.exe and sla.exe and is added to the user PATH, so the top-level sla command is available immediately after installation, with no need for SA_PLUGIN_DEV=1.
Source installation of the SLA pluginRun tools/install_windows.ps1 in the sa_plugin_sla directoryBuilds the plugin and registers it with the host, and also copies zig-out\bin\sla.exe into SCI's bin directory as the top-level command (a plugin installed via this path is in development mode).

Command list

CommandPurpose
sla init [path]Create a minimal SLA binary project skeleton.
sla check [file]Lexical / syntax / type checking, without emitting any assembly or SAB.
sla build [file]Compile a .sla file into verified .sa assembly text.
sla build-exe [file]By default takes the SA text path, emitting .sa and then compiling to a native executable, delegating to sa build-exe; only with an explicit --test-backend sab does it take the direct SAB path.
sla build-workspaceResolve member entry points according to the current sa.mod workspace, then compile to an executable.
sla sab build [file]Compile .sla to SAB bytes, written by default to the managed cache directory.
sla sab workspaceResolve workspace members, take the managed SAB compilation, then delegate to sa build-exe.
sla sab disasm <file.sab>Disassemble a SAB file for debugging; not part of the compilation path.
sla test [file]Compile a test file, then hand it to the host sa test to run.
sla skills [--json]List plugin capabilities, and optionally generate agent skill files.

General conventions

  • All commands accept -h / --help, write the usage line to stderr, and return 0; the usage line printed by the top-level sla --help lists both the sla <command> and sa sla <command> forms.
  • Commands that take an input file support both an explicit path and workspace mode: when the file argument is omitted, sa.mod is searched upward from the current directory, and the member's src/main.sla (or main.sla) is used as the entry point, with -p <package> selecting the member.
  • -p supports three forms: -p name, -p=name, and --package=name.
  • When delegating to the host sa build-exe / sa test, if the user has not explicitly given --jobs, the plugin automatically appends --jobs auto.

Quick start

After a formal installation (installer bundle or bundle script) no environment variables are needed at all; the complete loop:

# PowerShell / Git Bash 通用
sla init D:\tmp\sla_app
cd D:\tmp\sla_app
sla check src\main.sla
sla build src\main.sla --out D:\tmp\main.sa
sla build-exe src\main.sla -o D:\tmp\main.exe
D:\tmp\main.exe
# 源码开发态（--dev 安装的插件需要 SA_PLUGIN_DEV）
$env:SA_PLUGIN_DEV = "1"
sa sla init D:\tmp\sla_app
sa sla build-exe D:\tmp\sla_app\src\main.sla -o D:\tmp\main.exe

The content after this page expands command by command: first “init”, “check”, and “build”, then the explicit SAB entry point “sab” together with “build-exe” and “test”. The sa sla prefix in each page's title can likewise be replaced with the top-level sla.
